title: Egg Fried Rice
subtitle: Simple wok-fried rice with eggs and spring onion
excerpt: Egg fried rice is one of the fastest meals in the kitchen. Cold rice is the key. The technique is the same every time: very hot wok, quick movements, and nothing added until the previous step is done.
sourceNotes: Egg fried rice is a staple of Chinese home cooking and restaurant cooking worldwide. The dish has been adapted in every country it reached, but the fundamental technique of frying cold cooked rice with egg remains constant.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the rice the night before. Refrigerate uncovered to dry out.

content.text: Cold rice from the fridge is not optional here. Freshly cooked rice releases steam in the wok and turns the dish into a soggy mess.

items.prepNote: cooked the day before and refrigerated
sliced, white and green parts separated

content.text: Heat the wok over a high heat until just smoking.
Add 2 tablespoons of the oil. Add the white spring onion parts and garlic.
Add the remaining oil and the cold rice. Break up any clumps.
Fry for 3 minutes, pressing the rice against the wok to get some colour.
Add the peas. Stir for 1 minute.
Push the rice to the sides. Pour the beaten eggs into the centre of the wok.
Let the egg start to set for 20 seconds, then fold it through the rice.
Add the soy sauce and sesame oil. Toss to coat.
Scatter over the green spring onion tops. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Rice was fresh or the wok was not hot enough.
items.fix: Use cold day-old rice. Heat the wok until it smokes.

items.cause: Egg was left in the centre too long before folding in.
items.fix: Fold after 20 seconds while the egg is still slightly wet.

items.cause: Not enough soy sauce or no seasoning on the rice.
items.fix: Taste and add more soy sauce a teaspoon at a time.
